lessons.title: ECG Interpretation: จากไฟฟ้าหัวใจสู่การตัดสินใจ
lessons.summary: บทเรียนแบบเป็นระบบตั้งแต่ conduction system, ECG paper, rate/rhythm/axis/intervals จนถึง ischemia, conduction disease และการเชื่อม ECG กับ hemodynamics.

sections.title: 1) Electrical foundation
paragraphs: SA node เป็น pacemaker หลัก กระแสไฟผ่าน atria → AV node → His bundle → bundle branches → Purkinje. ECG เป็นภาพรวมของ depolarization/repolarization บนผิวกาย จึงต้องอ่านร่วมกับ physiology ไม่ใช่ดู pattern แยกจากคนไข้.
bullets: P wave = atrial depolarization
PR interval = atrial-to-ventricular conduction time
QRS = ventricular depolarization
ST-T = ventricular repolarization

sections.title: 2) ECG paper & calibration
paragraphs: มาตรฐานทั่วไป 25 mm/s และ 10 mm/mV. ที่ 25 mm/s: small box 0.04 s, large box 0.20 s. ก่อนตีความทุกครั้งให้ดู calibration, artifact และ lead reversal.
bullets: Regular rhythm: 300 ÷ จำนวน large boxes ระหว่าง R-R เป็นการประมาณ rate
Irregular rhythm: นับ QRS ใน 10 s ×6
QRS ≥120 ms = wide complex

sections.title: 3) Systematic reading sequence
paragraphs: ใช้ลำดับเดิมทุกครั้งเพื่อลด omission: Clinical context → Rhythm → Rate → Axis → P wave → PR → QRS width/morphology → QT/QTc → ST-T → comparison with old ECG.
bullets: Rhythm: regular/irregular, P before every QRS?, QRS after every P?
Axis: ดู I และ aVF เป็น screening แล้วค่อยละเอียดขึ้นเมื่อจำเป็น
Intervals: PR 120–200 ms โดยประมาณ, QRS <120 ms ใน conduction ปกติ
QTc ต้องตีความตาม rate และบริบท เช่น electrolyte/drug effects

sections.title: 4) Ischemia / infarction thinking
paragraphs: อย่าเริ่มจากคำว่า STEMI อย่างเดียว ให้ถามว่ามี acute coronary occlusion/ischemia หรือไม่และมี reciprocal change หรือ pattern high-risk หรือไม่.
bullets: Inferior: II, III, aVF; reciprocal change มักเห็นที่ I/aVL
Anterior/septal: V1–V4; lateral: I, aVL, V5–V6
Posterior MI อาจเป็น ST depression V1–V3 + tall R; พิจารณา V7–V9
Inferior MI ควรคิด RV involvement และพิจารณา V3R/V4R ตามระบบ

sections.title: 5) Wide complex & conduction disease
paragraphs: Wide-complex tachycardia ในผู้ใหญ่โดยเฉพาะมี structural heart disease ให้คิด VT ไว้ก่อนจนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ได้. AV block ต้องแยก 1st degree, Mobitz I, Mobitz II และ complete heart block โดยดู P-QRS relationship.
bullets: Unstable rhythm = treatment priority over perfect rhythm naming
QRS morphology, AV dissociation, capture/fusion beats ช่วยสนับสนุน VT
Hyperkalemia, sodium-channel blockade และ pacing สามารถทำให้ QRS กว้างได้

sections.title: 6) How to write an ECG impression
paragraphs: รายงานให้สั้นแต่ครบ: rhythm + rate + axis + interval + QRS + ischemic/conduction findings + clinical implication. ตัวอย่าง: 'Sinus rhythm ~60/min, narrow QRS, inferior ST elevation II/III/aVF with reciprocal depression I/aVL; concern for inferior OMI/STEMI, correlate symptoms and obtain right-sided leads.'

key_points: อ่านด้วยลำดับคงที่ทุกครั้ง
ECG เป็น data point ไม่ใช่ diagnosis เดี่ยว ๆ
Hemodynamic instability มีผลต่อการตัดสินใจมากกว่าความสวยงามของ ECG label
อย่าพลาด lead reversal/artifact ก่อนประกาศ arrhythmia
quick_review: I + aVF ช่วย screen axis
Wide complex tachycardia + instability → treat first

research_updates.title: Learning focus: OMI concepts continue to influence ECG education
research_updates.takeaway: Contemporary ECG education increasingly emphasizes recognizing acute coronary occlusion patterns beyond classic ST-elevation criteria, but local activation pathways still follow formal ACS/STEMI protocols.

actions.label: เปิด ECG Quick Reference

quiz.q: ลำดับที่ช่วยลด omission มากที่สุดคือข้อใด?
quiz.explain: ลำดับคงที่ช่วยลดการข้ามองค์ประกอบสำคัญและต้องผูกกับ clinical context.

quiz.q: ST elevation II, III, aVF สื่อถึง territory ใด?
quiz.explain: II, III, aVF เป็น inferior leads.

quiz.q: Wide-complex tachycardia ในผู้ป่วย unstable ควรทำอย่างไร?
options: รอ ECG 12 lead สมบูรณ์ก่อน
ให้ treatment ตาม unstable tachy pathway และคิด VT ไว้ก่อน
ให้ adenosine ทุกคน
quiz.explain: ความไม่คงที่ทาง hemodynamics เป็น priority.

lessons.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome: Pathophysiology → ECG → Prehospital System
lessons.summary: ACS ครอบคลุม unstable angina, NSTEMI และ STEMI/acute coronary occlusion. เป้าหมาย EMS คือจำแนก high-risk, ทำ ECG เร็ว, ให้การรักษาที่มีข้อบ่งชี้ และลดเวลาถึง reperfusion.

sections.title: 1) Pathophysiology
paragraphs: Plaque disruption/erosion → platelet activation → thrombus → supply-demand mismatch หรือ acute coronary occlusion. ระดับ ischemia ขึ้นกับตำแหน่งหลอดเลือด, collateral flow, duration และ myocardial demand.
bullets: Ischemia อาจ transient หรือ dynamic
Troponin บอก myocardial injury แต่ prehospital decision จำนวนมากต้องเริ่มก่อน lab
Mechanical/electrical complications อาจเกิดเร็ว เช่น VT/VF, AV block, pulmonary edema, shock

sections.title: 2) History & risk framing
paragraphs: Chest pressure/heaviness ร้าวแขน/กราม, diaphoresis, dyspnea, nausea เป็น classic แต่ atypical presentation พบได้ โดยเฉพาะสูงอายุ เบาหวาน และผู้หญิง.
bullets: OPQRST + SAMPLE
ถาม bleeding risk/anticoagulant/allergy
คิด aortic syndrome, PE, pneumothorax, esophageal cause, pericarditis และอื่น ๆ ก่อนผูกกับ ACS

sections.title: 3) ECG strategy
paragraphs: ทำ 12-lead เร็วและทำ serial ECG เมื่ออาการ/ECG เปลี่ยน. Inferior pattern ให้คิด RV infarct; posterior clues ให้คิด posterior leads.
bullets: Compare old ECG if available
Dynamic ST-T change เพิ่มความน่าเชื่อถือของ acute ischemia
Normal first ECG ไม่ได้ตัด ACS

sections.title: 4) Prehospital treatment principles
paragraphs: 2025 ACS guideline: oxygen แนะนำเมื่อ SpO₂ <90% เพื่อเพิ่ม saturation ≥90%; routine oxygen เมื่อ saturation ≥90% ไม่แนะนำเพราะไม่เพิ่ม cardiovascular outcomes.
bullets: Aspirin/antiplatelet strategy ต้องตาม local protocol/contraindications
Nitrates/analgesia ต้องดู BP, RV infarction, PDE-5 use และ local protocol
Transport destination/activation มีผลต่อ time-to-reperfusion

sections.title: 5) Complications & red flags
paragraphs: Inferior MI อาจเกิด brady/AV block; anterior large infarct เสี่ยง cardiogenic shock; ongoing chest pain + hypotension + pulmonary edema/arrhythmia เป็น high-risk.

key_points: ทำ 12-lead เร็วและ repeat เมื่อ clinical picture ยังน่าสงสัย
Oxygen ไม่ใช่ routine ใน normoxic ACS
รักษาและ transport เป็นระบบเวลา-sensitive
คิด differential รุนแรงเสมอ
quick_review: ACS + SpO₂ ≥90% → ไม่ให้ออกซิเจน routine
Inferior MI → right-sided leads when indicated
Normal ECG ครั้งแรก ≠ ACS excluded
red_flags: Sustained VT/VF or high-grade AV block
pitfalls: ให้ออกซิเจน routine ทั้งที่ normoxic
ตัด ACS จาก ECG แรกปกติ
ลืม RV/posterior leads เมื่อมีข้อบ่งชี้

research_updates.title: ACS guideline consolidated STEMI + NSTEMI evidence
research_updates.takeaway: The 2025 guideline replaced the separated older STEMI/NSTEMI frameworks with one ACS guideline and updates antiplatelet, invasive strategy and supportive-care recommendations.

research_updates.title: Routine oxygen in normoxic ACS
research_updates.takeaway: Randomized evidence reviewed in the 2025 guideline shows no cardiovascular benefit from routine oxygen when SpO₂ is already ≥90%.

actions.label: เปิด ECG Quick Reference

quiz.q: 2025 ACS guideline แนะนำ oxygen routine เมื่อ SpO₂ 97% หรือไม่?
options: แนะนำทุกคน
ไม่แนะนำ routine
ให้ 15 L/min เสมอ
ขึ้นกับอายุเท่านั้น
quiz.explain: Routine oxygen เมื่อ saturation ≥90% ไม่ได้เพิ่ม cardiovascular outcomes.

quiz.q: Inferior ST elevation ควรคิด lead เพิ่มใด?
options: aVR เท่านั้น
V1R เท่านั้น
quiz.explain: Right-sided leads เช่น V3R/V4R ช่วยประเมิน RV involvement.

lessons.title: Bradycardia & Tachyarrhythmia: Hemodynamics ก่อนชื่อ rhythm
lessons.summary: เป้าหมายคือประเมิน perfusion/instability, แยก narrow vs wide, regular vs irregular และรักษาตาม physiology ก่อนพยายามตั้งชื่อ rhythm แบบละเอียด.

sections.title: 1) Instability framework
paragraphs: Signs of poor perfusion ได้แก่ hypotension, altered mental status, ischemic chest discomfort, acute heart failure/shock. ถ้ามี instability จาก arrhythmia จริง ให้ electrical therapy ตาม algorithm เร็ว.
bullets: Brady: หาสาเหตุ hypoxia, ischemia, drugs, electrolyte, conduction disease
Tachy: narrow/wide + regular/irregular + stable/unstable

sections.title: 2) Adult bradycardia
paragraphs: AHA 2025 adult brady algorithm ใช้ atropine 1 mg IV bolus; repeat every 3–5 min, max 3 mg. ถ้า ineffective ให้พิจารณา transcutaneous pacing และ/หรือ dopamine/epinephrine infusion ตาม algorithm/local protocol.

sections.title: 3) Adult tachycardia
paragraphs: Unstable tachycardia → synchronized cardioversion. Stable narrow regular SVT → vagal maneuvers/adenosine when appropriate. Wide-complex tachycardia ต้องระวัง VT; irregular wide-complex อาจเป็น pre-excited AF และ adenosine/AV-nodal blockers อาจอันตรายในบางบริบท.

sections.title: 4) Pediatric differences
paragraphs: Pediatric bradycardia มัก secondary to hypoxia/respiratory failure มากกว่ primary conduction disease. หาก HR <60/min พร้อม cardiopulmonary compromise แม้ ventilation/oxygenation effective แล้ว ให้เริ่ม CPR ตาม PALS.
bullets: SVT stable: vagal → adenosine if IV/IO available
SVT unstable: synchronized cardioversion starting 0.5–1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg if unsuccessful

sections.title: 5) Post-conversion
paragraphs: หลัง rhythm conversion ต้องหาสาเหตุ, repeat ECG, monitor recurrence, electrolyte/glucose, medication/toxin and ischemia evaluation.

key_points: Treat the patient, not only the monitor
Wide complex tachycardia: assume VT until proven otherwise when uncertain
quick_review: Peds HR <60 + compromise despite oxygenation → CPR
SVT unstable peds: 0.5–1 then 2 J/kg cardioversion

research_updates.title: PALS bradycardia evidence remains low certainty
research_updates.takeaway: 2025 PALS reinforces ventilation-first thinking and CPR when HR <60/min with compromise despite effective ventilation; much of bradycardia evidence remains observational.

quiz.q: เด็ก brady HR 50/min มี shock despite effective ventilation ควรคิดอะไรต่อ?
quiz.explain: PALS recommends CPR for HR <60/min with cardiopulmonary compromise despite effective ventilation with oxygen.

quiz.q: Unstable adult tachyarrhythmia treatment priority?
quiz.explain: Unstable tachyarrhythmia should receive synchronized cardioversion according to algorithm.

lessons.title: Cardiac Arrest & Post-ROSC: CPR physiology, rhythms, drugs, EtCO₂
lessons.summary: เข้าใจเหตุผลของ high-quality CPR, shock timing, epinephrine, reversible causes, capnography และ post-ROSC care แทนการจำ algorithm อย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) CPR physiology
paragraphs: Chest compressions generate coronary/cerebral perfusion. Compression pauses rapidly reduce perfusion; minimizing interruptions is therefore central. Full recoil preserves venous return.
bullets: Adult rate 100–120/min
Adult depth at least 5 cm
Avoid excessive ventilation
Change compressor about every 2 min

sections.title: 2) Shockable vs non-shockable
paragraphs: VF/pVT: defibrillation is causal therapy; shock rapidly and resume CPR. PEA/asystole: prioritize CPR, epinephrine and reversible causes.
bullets: Epinephrine adult 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 min
Amiodarone/lidocaine considered in refractory VF/pVT
Hs & Ts guide reversible-cause search

sections.title: 3) Airway & capnography
paragraphs: Advanced airway should not delay initial CPR/defibrillation. Continuous waveform capnography is recommended to confirm/monitor ETT in adult arrest and can help assess CPR quality/trends.
bullets: Abrupt sustained rise in EtCO₂ may suggest ROSC
Persistently low/decreasing EtCO₂ → reassess CPR quality and other causes, not a stand-alone termination rule

sections.title: 4) Post-ROSC priorities
paragraphs: Reassess oxygenation/ventilation, blood pressure/perfusion, 12-lead ECG, cause of arrest, temperature management and neurologic status. Avoid hyperoxia/hypoventilation extremes and treat shock.

key_points: Epinephrine ASAP in nonshockable pediatric arrest
quick_review: EtCO₂ trend can support CPR quality assessment

research_updates.title: Pediatric epinephrine timing
research_updates.takeaway: 2025 evidence update found observational data favoring earlier epinephrine for initial nonshockable pediatric arrest, while timing in shockable rhythms remains uncertain because defibrillation must remain the priority.

actions.label: เปิด Cardiac Arrest Algorithm

quiz.q: ใน VF/pVT priority คืออะไร?
quiz.explain: Rapid defibrillation is the priority for shockable arrest.

quiz.q: Continuous waveform capnography in adult arrest is useful mainly for?
quiz.explain: AHA recommends waveform capnography to confirm/monitor ETT and it can support CPR quality assessment.

lessons.title: Airway Assessment & Difficult Airway: Plan A/B/C/D
lessons.summary: คิด airway เป็น continuum ตั้งแต่ basic opening, suction, BVM, SGA, ETT จนถึง rescue airway โดยมี oxygenation เป็นเป้าหมาย ไม่ใช่การ “ต้องใส่ท่อให้ได้”.

sections.title: 1) Airway threat recognition
paragraphs: ดูเสียง/effort/mental status/secretions/blood/facial trauma. Stridor, gurgling, snoring, inability to handle secretions, progressive edema และ severe fatigue เป็น red flags.
bullets: Airway protection ≠ ventilation ≠ oxygenation; ประเมินแยกกัน
GCS อย่างเดียวไม่ควรเป็นข้อบ่งชี้เดี่ยวโดยไม่ดู airway reflex/trajectory/ventilation

sections.title: 2) Difficult airway predictors
paragraphs: LEMON ใช้เตือน difficult laryngoscopy; MOANS ช่วยคิด difficult BVM; RODS ใช้กับ SGA; SMART ใช้คิด surgical airway difficulty. สิ่งเหล่านี้ไม่ใช่ perfect scores แต่เป็น prompts ให้เตรียม backup.
bullets: Look externally
Evaluate 3-3-2
Mallampati where feasible
Obstruction/obesity
Neck mobility

sections.title: 3) Airway strategy
paragraphs: Plan A = optimized first attempt; Plan B = alternate device/SGA; Plan C = oxygenation rescue/BVM; Plan D = emergency front-of-neck accessตาม scope/protocol. ทุกขั้นต้องกำหนด trigger สำหรับ move on เพื่อไม่ fixation error.

sections.title: 4) Pre-intubation checklist
paragraphs: SOAP-ME: suction, oxygen, airway equipment, pharmacy, monitoring, equipment/backup. เพิ่ม hemodynamic optimization, position, preoxygenation and post-intubation plan.

key_points: Suction is a primary airway tool, not an afterthought
red_flags: Rapidly falling mental status with loss of airway protection

quiz.q: Airway success ที่สำคัญที่สุดคืออะไร?
quiz.explain: Airway management is about maintaining oxygenation/ventilation; ETT is one tool.

quiz.q: MOANS ใช้เตือนเรื่องใด?
quiz.explain: MOANS is a common mnemonic for difficult bag-mask ventilation.

lessons.title: Preoxygenation, BVM & Peri-intubation Oxygenation
lessons.summary: ช่วงอันตรายที่สุดของ intubation มักเป็น hypoxemia/hypotension ไม่ใช่แค่ laryngoscopy failure. บทนี้เน้นการสร้าง oxygen reserve, BVM technique และ peri-intubation physiology.

sections.title: 1) Why preoxygenation matters
paragraphs: Preoxygenation replaces nitrogen in functional residual capacity with oxygen to prolong safe apnea time. Patients with shunt physiology, obesity, pregnancy or severe hypoxemia desaturate much faster.

sections.title: 2) BVM technique
paragraphs: Use proper mask size, airway positioning, OPA/NPA when appropriate, two-hand mask seal with second rescuer squeezing bag if available. Watch chest rise and avoid excessive pressure/volume.
bullets: Jaw thrust/chin lift as appropriate
PEEP can help selected hypoxemic patients
Suction before and during ventilation if contaminated

sections.title: 3) Apneic oxygenation & positive pressure
paragraphs: Nasal oxygen during attempts may help selected patients, but does not replace ventilation when ventilation is needed. NIV/CPAP preoxygenation is useful in some severely hypoxemic patients if they can tolerate it and have no contraindication.

sections.title: 4) Hemodynamic preparation
paragraphs: Positive pressure and induction can reduce venous return and BP. Identify shock, optimize volume/vasopressor strategy per protocol, choose induction dose thoughtfully, and monitor closely.

key_points: BVM excellence is a core rescue skill
Avoid both hypoxia and excessive ventilation

research_updates.title: Bag-mask ventilation during intubation
research_updates.takeaway: A randomized trial in critically ill adults found bag-mask ventilation during the apneic period reduced severe hypoxemia without a clear increase in aspiration; application depends on aspiration risk and local airway practice.

quiz.q: ผู้ป่วย severe hypoxemia ก่อน intubation ควรคิดอะไร?
quiz.explain: Optimization before laryngoscopy reduces peri-intubation hypoxemia risk.

lessons.title: RSI / Tracheal Intubation: First-pass success, drugs, capnography
lessons.summary: RSI คือ controlled process: prepare → preoxygenate → optimize physiology → induce/paralyze → place → confirm → secure → post-intubation sedation/ventilation.

sections.title: 1) Indications & decision
paragraphs: Intubate when airway cannot be protected, oxygenation/ventilation cannot be maintained, anticipated deterioration requires definitive airway, or procedural need justifies risk. Avoid reflex intubation without considering BVM/SGA/NIV alternatives.

sections.title: 2) First-pass strategy
paragraphs: First-pass success matters because repeated attempts increase hypoxemia, aspiration and trauma. Optimize operator/device/position/bougie/suction before starting.

sections.title: 3) Video vs direct laryngoscopy
paragraphs: DEVICE trial in critically ill adults showed higher first-attempt success with video laryngoscopy (85.1% vs 70.8%) without reduction in severe complication rate, supporting VL when equipment/training are available.
bullets: VL does not eliminate need for DL skills
Screen view can be excellent while tube delivery remains difficult—optimize stylet/bougie technique

sections.title: 4) Confirmation
paragraphs: Continuous waveform capnography + clinical assessment is the most reliable confirmation/monitoring method in adult arrest. Reconfirm after movement and if waveform/ventilation changes.

sections.title: 5) Post-intubation care
paragraphs: Tube fixation, analgesia/sedation, ventilator/BVM settings, BP monitoring, EtCO₂ trend and repeat auscultation are part of the procedure—not optional afterthoughts.

key_points: First attempt should be best attempt
Do not let intubation interrupt CPR excessively
quick_review: VL improves first-pass success in DEVICE trial

research_updates.title: DEVICE randomized trial
research_updates.takeaway: Video laryngoscopy improved first-attempt intubation success from 70.8% to 85.1% in critically ill adults; severe complications were similar.

quiz.q: DEVICE trial primary finding?
quiz.explain: First-attempt success was higher with video laryngoscopy.

quiz.q: Most reliable ETT confirmation adjunct in adult arrest?
quiz.explain: AHA recommends continuous waveform capnography in addition to clinical assessment.

lessons.title: Acute Respiratory Failure: Asthma, COPD, Pulmonary Edema, Pneumonia
lessons.summary: เรียนแบบ physiology-first: oxygenation failure, ventilation failure, work of breathing และ impending fatigue แล้วค่อยแยกโรค.

sections.title: 1) Respiratory failure framework
paragraphs: Type 1 = hypoxemic failure; Type 2 = hypercapnic/ventilatory failure. ผู้ป่วยอาจมีทั้งสอง. ดู mental status, respiratory effort, speech, air entry, SpO₂ และ capnography/ABG when available.
bullets: Silent chest + fatigue = late ominous sign
Normal SpO₂ ไม่ได้ยืนยัน ventilation ปกติ
Rising CO₂ + declining effort can indicate fatigue

sections.title: 2) Asthma/COPD
paragraphs: Bronchospasm causes expiratory flow limitation and dynamic hyperinflation. Prioritize bronchodilation, oxygen to target, steroids per protocol and avoid excessive ventilation if mechanically ventilating severe obstruction.
bullets: Look for prior ICU/intubation
Beware air trapping/auto-PEEP
A suddenly quiet chest can mean worsening obstruction, not improvement

sections.title: 3) Cardiogenic pulmonary edema
paragraphs: Acute pulmonary edema is a pressure/volume problem causing alveolar flooding and severe work of breathing. CPAP/NIV can improve oxygenation and reduce preload/afterload in appropriate conscious patients; nitrates/other therapy depend on BP/local protocol.

sections.title: 4) Pneumonia/other parenchymal disease
paragraphs: Shunt physiology may make simple oxygen less effective; positioning, high-flow/NIV or intubation may be required depending on trajectory and resources.

key_points: Assess work of breathing, not SpO₂ alone
Ventilation failure can exist with acceptable saturation
NIV is powerful but requires cooperation and airway protection
quick_review: Pulmonary edema: think CPAP/NIV if appropriate

quiz.q: SpO₂ 98% แต่ผู้ป่วยซึมและ hypoventilate สามารถมี respiratory failure ได้หรือไม่?
quiz.explain: SpO₂ reflects oxygenation, not ventilation/CO₂ clearance.

lessons.title: Pediatric Systematic Assessment: PAT → ABCDE → SAMPLE
lessons.summary: เด็ก decompensate ได้เร็วและ hypotension เป็น late sign. ใช้ appearance/work of breathing/circulation + primary assessment เพื่อตีความ physiology ก่อน diagnosis.

sections.title: 1) Pediatric Assessment Triangle
paragraphs: PAT = Appearance + Work of Breathing + Circulation to skin. เป็น rapid visual/auditory impression ไม่ต้องใช้อุปกรณ์ และช่วย classify respiratory distress/failure, shock or CNS/metabolic problem.

sections.title: 2) Primary assessment
paragraphs: A/B/C/D/E พร้อม age-appropriate vitals. HR/RR/BP ต้องตีความตามอายุและ context. Cap refill/peripheral pulse/mental status ช่วยเมื่อ BP ยังปกติ.
bullets: Hypotension = decompensated shock until proven otherwise
Bradycardia in sick child often points to hypoxia/late deterioration

sections.title: 3) Secondary assessment
paragraphs: SAMPLE + focused history: feeding/urine, fever, seizure, birth/prematurity, congenital heart disease, toxin/medication, trauma, immunization depending on case.

sections.title: 4) Reassessment
paragraphs: เด็กเปลี่ยนเร็ว จึงต้อง trend mental status, WOB, HR, perfusion, SpO₂, glucose and response to intervention rather than relying on one snapshot.

quick_review: Check glucose early in altered child

quiz.q: Hypotension ในเด็กมักเป็น early หรือ late sign ของ shock?
quiz.explain: Children can compensate with tachycardia/vasoconstriction until later decompensation.

lessons.title: Pediatric Arrest & Shock: ventilation-first physiology, epinephrine, defibrillation
lessons.summary: เด็ก arrest มักเริ่มจาก respiratory failure/shock. หัวใจของ PALS คือ prevention, ventilation/oxygenation, CPR quality, timely defibrillation และ weight-based dosing.

sections.title: 1) Arrest prevention
paragraphs: Recognize respiratory failure and shock before pulseless arrest. Correct hypoxia, support ventilation, obtain vascular access when needed and treat underlying cause.

sections.title: 2) CPR/defibrillation
paragraphs: Compression 100–120/min, depth ≥1/3 AP diameter. Shockable arrest: 2 J/kg → 4 J/kg → subsequent ≥4 J/kg up to 10 J/kg or adult dose.
bullets: Advanced airway: continuous compressions + breath every 2–3 s
Monitor EtCO₂ and invasive diastolic BP when available

sections.title: 3) Epinephrine & antiarrhythmics
paragraphs: Nonshockable pediatric arrest: initial epinephrine as early as possible. Shockable rhythm: prioritize defibrillation; epinephrine may be given after 2 shocks or earlier if rapid defibrillation is not possible.
bullets: Epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (0.1 mg/mL), max 1 mg
Amiodarone 5 mg/kg or lidocaine 1 mg/kg for shock-refractory VF/pVT

sections.title: 4) Shock types
paragraphs: Hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic and obstructive shock require different resuscitation. Fluid volume/rate should reflect cause and response; cardiogenic shock can worsen with indiscriminate large boluses.

key_points: Early epinephrine matters in nonshockable arrest
Avoid routine calcium/bicarbonate unless special indication

research_updates.title: Earlier epinephrine in nonshockable pediatric arrest
research_updates.takeaway: Evidence updates identified observational studies linking shorter time to first epinephrine with better outcomes in nonshockable arrest; certainty remains limited.

quiz.q: Initial nonshockable pediatric arrest: epinephrine timing?
quiz.explain: 2025 PALS supports early epinephrine for nonshockable arrest.

quiz.q: Routine calcium in pediatric arrest?
quiz.explain: Routine calcium is not recommended except specific indications such as hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia or CCB overdose.

lessons.title: Pediatric Bradycardia, SVT & Wide-Complex Tachycardia
lessons.summary: Arrhythmia ในเด็กต้องเริ่มจาก perfusion/respiratory status. Bradycardia ส่วนใหญ่ secondary; tachycardia ต้องแยก sinus tachycardia, SVT และ wide-complex rhythms.

sections.title: 1) Bradycardia
paragraphs: Correct hypoxia/ventilation first. If HR <60/min with cardiopulmonary compromise despite effective ventilation with oxygen → start CPR. Epinephrine IV/IO if persistent after correction. Atropine for increased vagal tone/primary AV block.

sections.title: 2) SVT
paragraphs: SVT often regular narrow complex, abrupt onset, rate often very high for age. Stable → vagal then adenosine if access available. Unstable → synchronized cardioversion starting 0.5–1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg.

sections.title: 3) Wide-complex tachycardia
paragraphs: Consider VT vs SVT with aberrancy; if unstable cardiovert. Stable wide-complex requires expert guidance and careful drug selection; avoid reflex AV nodal blockade in pre-excitation contexts.

key_points: Unstable SVT/VT with pulse: synchronized cardioversion

quiz.q: Atropine เหมาะที่สุดใน pediatric brady แบบใด?
options: Increased vagal tone or primary AV block
quiz.explain: 2025 PALS limits atropine use to vagal tone/AV conduction block contexts rather than hypoxic bradycardia.

lessons.title: Neonatal Transition & Initial Steps: first minute matters
lessons.summary: Neonatal resuscitation differs from PALS: most bradycardia at birth is due to ineffective ventilation/gas exchange. Effective lung inflation is the central intervention.

sections.title: 1) Transition physiology
paragraphs: At birth pulmonary vascular resistance falls, lungs aerate and oxygen saturation rises gradually over minutes. Newborn targets are therefore lower than older children/adults in the first minutes.

sections.title: 2) Initial questions
paragraphs: Term gestation? good tone? breathing/crying? If yes → routine care/temperature/ongoing evaluation. If no → warm, dry, position, stimulate, clear airway only if needed.

sections.title: 3) When to ventilate
paragraphs: Apnea/gasping or HR <100/min → begin positive-pressure ventilation promptly. Rise in heart rate is the best indicator of effective ventilation.

sections.title: 4) Oxygen strategy
paragraphs: 2025 AHA/AAP: term/late preterm ≥35 wk can reasonably start respiratory support with 21% O₂; 32–34+6 wk 21–30%; <32 wk may need 30–100%, titrated to preductal SpO₂ targets.

key_points: HR response tells you if ventilation works

quiz.q: Key indicator of effective PPV in newborn?
quiz.explain: A rising heart rate is the primary indicator of effective ventilation.

lessons.title: Neonatal Ventilation, ETT, Laryngeal Mask & Video Laryngoscopy
lessons.summary: Airway newborn ต้องคิดตาม GA/weight, device availability และ ventilation effectiveness. New 2025 evidence strengthens the role of supraglottic airway and video laryngoscopy in selected settings.

sections.title: 1) Face-mask ventilation problems
paragraphs: Mask leak and airway obstruction are common. If HR stays <100/min despite PPV, perform corrective ventilation steps and consider alternative airway.

sections.title: 2) Laryngeal mask
paragraphs: 2025 guidance: laryngeal mask is reasonable as an alternative to ETT when face-mask ventilation fails in newborns ≥34 weeks, and may be reasonable as a primary ventilation interface in that group where training/resources support it.

sections.title: 3) ETT sizing & depth
paragraphs: Use GA/weight table rather than one universal formula. Prepare adjacent tube sizes and confirm depth by clinical response/exhaled CO₂ and local imaging where appropriate.

sections.title: 4) Video laryngoscopy evidence
paragraphs: ILCOR 2025 suggests video laryngoscopy over traditional laryngoscopy where resources/training allow, especially for less-experienced clinicians. Meta-analysis of RCTs showed higher overall and first-attempt success.

sections.title: 5) Blade selection
paragraphs: Straight Miller-type blades are standard neonatal tools; #00 for extremely preterm/small infants in some systems, #0 for preterm, #1 for term/larger infants, but exact device choice should follow local equipment and training.

key_points: Video laryngoscopy improves first-attempt success in neonatal evidence
quick_review: Preterm often Miller 0; term often Miller 1

research_updates.title: Neonatal video laryngoscopy evidence
research_updates.takeaway: Across 4 RCTs, video laryngoscopy increased overall and first-attempt intubation success; ILCOR 2025 conditionally favors VL where resources/training permit.

research_updates.title: NICU quality improvement with VL
research_updates.takeaway: A 2026 QI project reported sustained improvement in first-attempt success after implementing VL and standardized oxygenation, including infants <1000 g.

quiz.q: 2025 neonatal guidance supports laryngeal mask most clearly in which group?
quiz.explain: Evidence and recommendations are strongest for newborns ≥34 weeks.

quiz.q: 2025 neonatal evidence for video laryngoscopy?
quiz.explain: RCT evidence summarized by ILCOR showed improved first-attempt success.

lessons.title: Advanced Neonatal Resuscitation: compressions, epinephrine, volume, post-care
lessons.summary: เมื่อ HR ยัง <60/min หลัง ventilation ที่ทำให้ chest movement แล้ว ให้ escalate อย่างเป็นลำดับ: alternative airway → compressions 3:1 → oxygen/vascular access → epinephrine → causes/volume.

sections.title: 1) Chest compressions
paragraphs: If HR remains <60/min despite 30 s effective ventilation, provide chest compressions. Preferred technique = two-thumb encircling hands, ratio 3:1 with ventilation.

sections.title: 2) Epinephrine
paragraphs: If HR remains <60/min despite 60 s compressions + adequate ventilation, give intravascular epinephrine 0.01–0.03 mg/kg. ET epinephrine 0.05–0.1 mg/kg may be used while obtaining vascular access. Repeat q3–5 min if needed.

sections.title: 3) Vascular access
paragraphs: Low-lying umbilical venous catheter is preferred; IO may be considered when IV/UVC not feasible, depending on setting and expertise.

sections.title: 4) Volume expansion
paragraphs: When blood loss/hypovolemia is suspected and there is inadequate response to epinephrine, volume expansion is indicated; choice/volume follow neonatal/local protocol.

sections.title: 5) Postresuscitation
paragraphs: Monitor glucose, temperature, oxygenation/ventilation, neurologic status and complications after prolonged ventilation/advanced resuscitation.

quiz.q: Neonatal compressions start after?
quiz.explain: Effective ventilation must be established first; compressions are for persistent HR <60/min.

lessons.title: Trauma XABCDE & Hemorrhage Control
lessons.summary: เป้าหมาย trauma resuscitation คือแก้ immediate killers ตามลำดับ โดยเฉพาะ catastrophic hemorrhage, airway compromise, tension physiology และ shock ขณะลด scene time ที่ไม่จำเป็น.

sections.title: 1) X — exsanguination
paragraphs: Control catastrophic external bleeding immediately: direct pressure, wound packing/hemostatic gauze, tourniquet when indicated. Reassess bleeding after movement/transport.

sections.title: 2) A/B
paragraphs: Airway with C-spine consideration when mechanism/assessment indicates. Breathing: identify tension pneumothorax, open pneumothorax, massive hemothorax, flail/chest wall injury and ventilatory failure.

sections.title: 3) C — perfusion
paragraphs: Assess pulse quality, skin, mental status, BP trend and shock index. Avoid spending scene time on interventions that do not change immediate survival/transport priority.

sections.title: 4) D/E
paragraphs: GCS/pupils/glucose when indicated. Fully expose enough to find injury while actively preventing hypothermia because hypothermia worsens coagulopathy.

sections.title: 5) Handover
paragraphs: MIST/ATMIST should transmit mechanism, injuries/findings, vital trends and treatment/response—not just single vital values.

key_points: X before A when catastrophic hemorrhage

quiz.q: Massive external hemorrhage in XABCDE ถูกจัดการเมื่อใด?
quiz.explain: Catastrophic hemorrhage is the X priority before standard ABCDE.

lessons.title: Traumatic Brain Injury: prevent secondary brain injury
lessons.summary: TBI outcome is heavily influenced by secondary insults—especially hypoxemia, hypotension, abnormal ventilation and delayed definitive care.

sections.title: 1) Primary vs secondary injury
paragraphs: Primary injury occurs at impact; secondary injury evolves through ischemia, edema, excitotoxicity and impaired autoregulation. EMS cannot reverse primary injury but can prevent secondary insults.

sections.title: 2) Oxygenation/ventilation
paragraphs: Avoid SpO₂ <90%. Establish airway if severe TBI with inability to protect airway or refractory hypoxemia. After intubation, monitor EtCO₂; avoid routine hyperventilation. BTF prehospital guidance targets normal ventilation, often EtCO₂ 35–40 mmHg, unless signs of herniation justify temporary hyperventilation per protocol.

sections.title: 3) Blood pressure
paragraphs: Hypotension worsens cerebral ischemia. Severe TBI guidelines suggest age-based higher SBP targets in adults; prehospital teams should avoid hypotension and treat shock while minimizing delay.

sections.title: 4) Neuro exam
paragraphs: Trend GCS and pupils after ABC stabilization and preferably before sedative/paralytic drugs. Document lateralizing signs and changes over time.

sections.title: 5) Destination
paragraphs: Severe TBI benefits from trauma/neurosurgical capability. Transport strategy should minimize total time to CT/neurosurgical care.

research_updates.title: BTF prehospital TBI 3rd edition
research_updates.takeaway: The Brain Trauma Foundation now lists a 3rd edition prehospital guideline framework covering oxygenation, BP, ventilation, GCS, pupils, fluids, hyperosmolar therapy and destination decisions.

sources.label: Brain Trauma Foundation Prehospital TBI Guidelines

quiz.q: Routine prophylactic hyperventilation in severe TBI?
quiz.explain: Routine hyperventilation can reduce cerebral blood flow and is avoided except selected herniation contexts.

lessons.title: Chest Trauma: tension pneumothorax, hemothorax, flail chest, tamponade
lessons.summary: Chest trauma kills through ventilation failure and obstructive/hemorrhagic shock. Diagnosis is primarily clinical in the unstable patient.

sections.title: 1) Tension pneumothorax
paragraphs: Think respiratory distress, unilateral reduced breath sounds, shock/obstructive physiology; late tracheal deviation is not required. Immediate decompression follows local scope/protocol when clinically suspected in an unstable patient.

sections.title: 2) Open pneumothorax
paragraphs: Manage open chest wound with appropriate vented/occlusive strategy per protocol while watching for tension development.

sections.title: 3) Massive hemothorax
paragraphs: Causes both blood loss and impaired ventilation. Look for shock + decreased breath sounds/dullness; definitive treatment requires chest drainage/surgery at hospital.

sections.title: 4) Tamponade / blunt cardiac injury
paragraphs: Tamponade may present with obstructive shock but classic Beck triad is often incomplete in trauma. ECG/ultrasound can support diagnosis; rapid transport/definitive intervention matters.

key_points: Clinical deterioration can precede textbook signs
Tension pneumothorax is a clinical emergency
Chest injury can cause both respiratory and circulatory failure
quick_review: Unilateral breath loss + shock = tension until proven otherwise in the right context

quiz.q: Tracheal deviation จำเป็นต้องมีเพื่อวินิจฉัย tension pneumothorax หรือไม่?
options: ไม่จำเป็น เป็น late sign
quiz.explain: Diagnosis in unstable trauma is clinical; late textbook signs may be absent.

lessons.title: Hemorrhagic Shock & Prehospital Blood: what is changing?
lessons.summary: การ resuscitate hemorrhage เปลี่ยนจาก crystalloid-heavy ไปสู่ early blood component/whole blood strategies ใน systems ที่พร้อม โดยต้อง balance evidence, logistics, safety and local protocol.

sections.title: 1) Hemorrhagic shock physiology
paragraphs: Loss of circulating volume reduces preload and oxygen delivery; compensatory vasoconstriction/tachycardia may mask severity. Lactate/mental status/skin/pulse/BP trends help assess perfusion.

sections.title: 2) Why blood rather than large crystalloid volumes
paragraphs: Large crystalloid volumes can worsen dilution, edema, hypothermia and coagulopathy. Modern trauma systems increasingly prioritize blood products when available for severe hemorrhagic shock.

sections.title: 3) Prehospital whole blood
paragraphs: Implementation requires cold chain, donor/product policy, transfusion reactions preparedness and clear activation criteria. Evidence is evolving and system-specific.

key_points: Whole blood programs require system infrastructure

research_updates.title: TOWAR prehospital whole blood trial
research_updates.takeaway: A large pragmatic cluster-randomized phase 3 trial compared up to 2 units of whole blood with component therapy in prehospital trauma hemorrhage, reflecting the rapid maturation of prehospital transfusion systems. Interpret outcomes in context of local capability and protocol.

quiz.q: Large-volume crystalloid in hemorrhagic shock can worsen?
quiz.explain: Excess crystalloid may worsen dilution, hypothermia and coagulopathy.

lessons.title: Acute Ischemic Stroke 2026: EMS triage, TNK, thrombectomy & time windows
lessons.summary: 2026 AHA/ASA guideline updates the full stroke pathway from prehospital evaluation through acute treatment, with broader thrombectomy eligibility and stronger systems-of-care emphasis.

sections.title: 1) Prehospital recognition
paragraphs: Use validated stroke recognition, establish last known well, glucose, anticoagulant history, baseline function and rapid destination decision. BE-FAST helps capture posterior symptoms but should not replace local stroke scale/pathway.

sections.title: 2) Time & imaging
paragraphs: Do not delay transport for unnecessary interventions. In-hospital imaging determines hemorrhage, LVO and thrombolysis/thrombectomy eligibility; prehospital notification helps shorten door-to-treatment times.

sections.title: 3) 2026 thrombolysis update
paragraphs: For eligible adults within 4.5 h, 2026 guideline recommends tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg. Extended-window thrombolysis may be reasonable in selected patients based on advanced imaging.

sections.title: 4) Thrombectomy expansion
paragraphs: Eligibility for EVT has broadened, including selected larger-core and posterior circulation/basilar occlusions, with recommendations extending to up to 24 h in defined populations.

sections.title: 5) Supportive care
paragraphs: Avoid hypoglycemia; treat severe abnormalities, monitor oxygenation/BP per stroke protocol, and avoid treatment that delays reperfusion.

quick_review: Do not delay definitive stroke pathway

research_updates.title: Major guideline update
research_updates.takeaway: 2026 AIS guidance endorses mobile stroke units, refines EMS triage, expands tenecteplase use and broadens EVT eligibility including basilar occlusion and selected larger-core patients.

quiz.q: 2026 AIS guideline recognizes which thrombolytic option within 4.5 h in eligible adults?
quiz.explain: The 2026 guideline recommends either TNK 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg in eligible adults.

lessons.title: Seizure, Status Epilepticus & Altered Mental Status
lessons.summary: ชักเป็น symptom ไม่ใช่ diagnosis. EMS ต้อง prioritize safety/ABC, duration, glucose, pregnancy/toxin/trauma, temperature and persistent altered state.

sections.title: 1) Seizure priorities
paragraphs: Protect from injury, position/suction airway as needed, monitor ventilation/oxygenation, obtain glucose and time the seizure. Do not restrain forcefully or place objects in the mouth.

sections.title: 2) Status / ongoing seizure
paragraphs: Persistent convulsive seizure is time-sensitive because longer duration increases treatment resistance and metabolic complications. Benzodiazepine route/dose must follow local protocol and available access.

sections.title: 3) Differential
paragraphs: Hypoglycemia, stroke/ICH, infection, eclampsia, toxin/withdrawal, electrolyte disturbance, trauma and psychogenic nonepileptic events are important differentials.

sections.title: 4) Post-ictal reassessment
paragraphs: Repeat neuro exam, vitals, glucose, trauma check and transport decision. Failure to regain expected mental status raises concern for nonconvulsive status, structural lesion or ongoing toxic/metabolic problem.

key_points: Persistent altered mental status needs reassessment

quiz.q: Early bedside test in altered/seizing patient?
quiz.explain: Hypoglycemia is rapidly reversible and must be checked early.

lessons.title: Shock Physiology: preload, pump, SVR and oxygen delivery
lessons.summary: เรียน shock โดยถาม 4 อย่าง: volume/preload, pump, vascular tone, obstruction. การรู้ physiology ช่วยเลือก fluid, vasopressor, ventilation and destination ได้ถูกกว่าใช้ BP อย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) Oxygen delivery
paragraphs: DO₂ ≈ cardiac output × arterial oxygen content. Cardiac output = HR × stroke volume; oxygen content depends heavily on hemoglobin and saturation. Normal BP ไม่ได้แปลว่า perfusion ปกติ.

sections.title: 2) Hypovolemic shock
paragraphs: Low preload from hemorrhage/dehydration. Treat source + appropriate volume/blood strategy. Hemorrhage requires bleeding control, not just fluid.

sections.title: 3) Distributive shock
paragraphs: Vasodilation/maldistribution (sepsis, anaphylaxis, neurogenic). Fluid and vasopressor needs depend on cause, response and local protocol.

sections.title: 4) Cardiogenic shock
paragraphs: Pump failure: MI, myocarditis, severe arrhythmia. Excess fluid can worsen pulmonary edema; consider vasoactive/inotropic support and reperfusion/definitive care.

sections.title: 5) Obstructive shock
paragraphs: Tension pneumothorax, tamponade, massive PE impair filling/outflow. Definitive relief of obstruction is key; fluids/pressors are temporizing.

key_points: Treat shock cause, not only number
quick_review: Trend mental status, pulse, skin, BP, lactate when available

quiz.q: Tension pneumothorax causes which shock type?
quiz.explain: Tension pneumothorax reduces venous return and causes obstructive shock.

lessons.title: Sepsis & Septic Shock 2026: recognition, source, fluids, vasopressors
lessons.summary: 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign updates adult sepsis guidance and explicitly includes the immediate prehospital setting. Early recognition, source-directed care and hemodynamic reassessment remain central.

sections.title: 1) What sepsis is
paragraphs: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response to infection. Do not equate fever + tachycardia alone with sepsis; look for organ dysfunction/perfusion failure.

sections.title: 2) Prehospital recognition
paragraphs: Suspect infection + altered mentation, hypotension, tachypnea, mottling, oliguria history, elevated lactate if available. qSOFA is not a stand-alone rule-out tool.

sections.title: 3) Resuscitation thinking
paragraphs: Give oxygen for hypoxemia, obtain IV/IO if indicated, fluid strategy should be individualized and reassessed frequently; persistent hypotension may require vasopressor support per system capability.

sections.title: 4) Source & antibiotics
paragraphs: Definitive sepsis care requires timely antimicrobials and source control, but prehospital protocols vary. Pre-notification can speed in-hospital bundle execution.

sections.title: 5) Reassessment
paragraphs: Reassess BP/MAP, mental status, capillary refill, urine history, lactate trend if measured, lung exam/ultrasound and signs of fluid intolerance.

key_points: Reassess after fluid rather than fixed-volume reflex
Prehospital recognition can shorten time to treatment
quick_review: Avoid fluid overload in poor cardiac reserve

research_updates.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign update
research_updates.takeaway: The 2026 SSC replaces 2021 guidance with 129 statements, including 46 new statements and explicit attention to immediate prehospital care.

quiz.q: 2026 SSC guideline scope includes?
options: Hospital + immediate prehospital and post-hospital settings
quiz.explain: The 2026 adult guideline explicitly includes the immediate prehospital setting.

lessons.title: Emergency Pharmacology & Medication Safety
lessons.summary: ความผิดพลาด EMS มักเกิดจาก concentration, decimal, weight, route หรือ unit ไม่ใช่การจำชื่อยาไม่ได้. บทนี้เน้นระบบป้องกัน error.

sections.title: 1) Dose language
paragraphs: แยก mg, mg/kg, mcg/kg/min, mL และ concentration ให้ชัด. คำนวณ dose ก่อน แล้วค่อยแปลงเป็น volume.

sections.title: 2) Weight-based dosing
paragraphs: ใช้ actual measured weight เมื่อเป็นไปได้. Estimated weight โดยเฉพาะ neonate/เด็กเล็กเป็น safety risk และต้อง double-check.

sections.title: 3) Concentration traps
paragraphs: Epinephrine เป็น classic high-risk example: concentration ต่างกันตาม indication/route. แอปต้องโชว์ mg และ mL พร้อม concentration ทุกครั้ง.

sections.title: 4) Independent double-check
paragraphs: High-alert medication ควร verbalize: patient weight, indication, dose, concentration, volume, route, max dose และ time given.

sections.title: 5) Infusions
paragraphs: ก่อนเริ่ม infusion ให้ยืนยัน drug amount, diluent volume, final concentration, dose unit, pump rate and compatible line.

key_points: Use leading zero; avoid trailing zero
quick_review: 0.1 mg ≠ 0.1 mL unless concentration says so

sources.label: AHA/AAP drug tables and local medication protocols

quiz.q: หลักที่ปลอดภัยที่สุดก่อนแปลงยาเป็น mL?
options: คำนวณ dose ที่ต้องการเป็น mg/mcg ก่อน
ใช้ mL อย่างเดียว
ไม่ต้องดู concentration
quiz.explain: Dose and concentration must be separated before calculating volume.

lessons.title: Obstetric Emergencies: PPH, eclampsia & cardiac arrest in pregnancy
lessons.summary: OB emergencies combine hemorrhage, airway difficulty, altered physiology and two-patient considerations. PPH and cardiac arrest are strongly time-sensitive.

sections.title: 1) Postpartum hemorrhage
paragraphs: PPH may occur without obvious risk factors. Quantify blood loss when possible, assess vitals/perfusion, uterine tone and source of bleeding. The 2025 WHO consolidated guideline emphasizes earlier recognition and rapid bundle-based treatment.

sections.title: 2) WHO 2025 MOTIVE bundle
paragraphs: Once PPH is diagnosed, WHO highlights immediate coordinated actions: uterine Massage, Oxytocic drugs, Tranexamic acid, IV fluids, Vaginal/genital tract examination, and Escalation of care.

sections.title: 3) TXA timing
paragraphs: WHO evidence supports early IV TXA for PPH as part of treatment; benefit decreases with delay and administration beyond 3 h after birth is not supported by the cited evidence. Local EMS scope/protocol determines prehospital use.

sections.title: 4) Pregnancy cardiac arrest
paragraphs: AHA 2025: standard high-quality CPR + continuous left lateral uterine displacement when fundus at/above umbilicus; prepare resuscitative delivery immediately with goal completion by 5 min if no ROSC, depending on resources.

sections.title: 5) Eclampsia
paragraphs: Pregnancy/postpartum seizure with hypertension features requires airway/oxygenation protection, magnesium-based treatment per obstetric protocol, BP management and rapid obstetric destination.

key_points: PPH requires early recognition and coordinated response
Pregnancy arrest: left uterine displacement + prepare delivery
Airway may be more difficult in pregnancy
quick_review: Goal resuscitative delivery by 5 min if no ROSC

research_updates.title: WHO consolidated PPH guideline
research_updates.takeaway: WHO/FIGO/ICM consolidated 51 evidence-based recommendations and emphasized earlier diagnosis and immediate MOTIVE bundle treatment.

quiz.q: WHO 2025 PPH bundle acronym includes TXA?
quiz.explain: Tranexamic acid is part of the MOTIVE bundle.

quiz.q: AHA pregnancy arrest target for resuscitative delivery if no ROSC?
quiz.explain: AHA 2025 recommends preparing immediately with a goal to complete by 5 minutes when indicated/resources allow.

lessons.title: Toxicology: toxidromes, cardiotoxic poisonings & special resuscitation
lessons.summary: Toxicology management starts with supportive ABC, glucose/temperature/ECG, pattern recognition and consultation—not antidote memorization alone.

sections.title: 1) Toxidrome approach
paragraphs: Sympathomimetic, anticholinergic, cholinergic, opioid, sedative-hypnotic and serotonin syndromes provide pattern recognition, but mixed ingestions are common.

sections.title: 2) ECG in poisoning
paragraphs: QRS widening, QT prolongation, AV block/bradycardia and ventricular dysrhythmia can guide urgency and toxin class. Sodium-channel blockers, TCAs and some antiarrhythmics are classic QRS-widening causes.

sections.title: 3) Supportive priorities
paragraphs: Airway/ventilation, seizure control, temperature, glucose, fluids/vasopressors and continuous ECG are often more important than a specific antidote early.

sections.title: 4) 2025 AHA special circumstances
paragraphs: Updated guidance covers opioid, beta-blocker, calcium-channel blocker, cocaine/sympathomimetic, cyanide, digoxin, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, methemoglobinemia, organophosphate/carbamate, sodium-channel blocker and hydrocarbon poisoning.

sections.title: 5) CCB poisoning example
paragraphs: 2025 AHA: high-dose insulin and vasopressors are recommended for hypotension in life-threatening CCB poisoning; calcium is reasonable, while glucagon usefulness is uncertain.

key_points: ECG is a toxicology vital sign
Call poison center/toxicology early when available

research_updates.title: Special circumstances guideline expansion
research_updates.takeaway: AHA 2025 updated 44 recommendations and added 140 new recommendations across special circumstances including multiple poisonings and pregnancy.

quiz.q: Life-threatening CCB poisoning with hypotension: 2025 AHA recommends?
quiz.explain: High-dose insulin and vasopressors are recommended for hypotension in life-threatening CCB poisoning.
